hook.line: A new SEO tactic people are doing: making pages with Reddit in the slug, title and H1.
hook.visual: Selfie-arm walking shot on a sunny street, bearded man close to camera, white three-line caption across his chest from frame one.

beats.what: Names the tactic in the first sentence: a new SEO trick, already mid-walk
Lists the three places 'Reddit' is stuffed: URL slug, page title, H1
Explains the target: the long searches ChatGPT and other LLMs run that contain 'Reddit'
Key twist: the LLM does not search Reddit itself, it searches Google plus the word 'Reddit'
Payoff: SEOs target those exact searches so their pages sit beside the Reddit results
Consequence: they can influence what the LLM answers
Closes with 'crazy tactic' and credits the SEO who shared it

why_it_works: One concrete, slightly sneaky trick named in the first five words, so SEO viewers stay to learn whether it works
Insider mechanism explained step by step (LLM searches Google plus 'Reddit'), giving the viewer something to repeat to colleagues, which drives the high share count
Single unbroken walking selfie (0 cuts in 42 s) feels like a friend telling you news, not a produced ad
Large three-line sentence captions over the chest let the whole argument be read with sound off
weaknesses: No visual proof: never shows an example page or an LLM answer, so the claim rests on his word
No cuts, zooms or graphics for 42 s; retention relies entirely on the idea
No CTA; ends on a credit line instead of asking for a follow or comment
for_robert: Steal the 'one new tactic, explained in one mechanism' structure, but add the proof he skips: have Fred hold up a pixel-art screenshot of the example search result at the twist moment.
